expected_findings.description: `swap_remove(pos)` moves the vector's last entry into slot `pos`, but nothing updates `index` for that moved entry. Its name still maps to the old final position, which is now out of range, so `addr_of` for it returns `None` even though `names()` still lists it. Once a later `insert` reuses that position the stale mapping resolves to a different service's address, and a later `remove` of the moved name deletes whichever entry now sits at the stale index. The `Vec::remove` version the change replaced kept the map consistent by renumbering every position above `pos`; the new version drops that pass without providing a replacement.

notes:
The defect is a broken invariant between two fields of the same struct: `entries` and `index` must agree on every name's position, and `swap_remove` breaks that agreement for exactly one entry — the one that was last.

The four unit tests in src/registry.rs survive the change because none of them removes an entry from the middle of a registry that still has entries after it. `deregistering_the_last_entry_shrinks_the_registry` removes "billing", which is the final element, and for the final element `swap_remove` and `remove` are identical operations; `deregistering_an_unknown_name_reports_false` never reaches the removal at all, and the other two tests never remove anything. A reviewer cannot rely on `cargo test` here: the suite passes and reports nothing.

Verified by execution: an integration test built the registry auth=10.0.0.1, billing=10.0.0.2, cache=10.0.0.3 and then removed "auth". Literal output:

    after remove("auth"): names = ["cache", "billing"]
      addr_of("cache") = None   [expected Some("10.0.0.3")]
    after insert("dns"): names = ["cache", "billing", "dns"]
      addr_of("cache") = Some("10.0.0.4")   [expected Some("10.0.0.3")]
    remove("cache") returned true
      names = ["billing", "dns"] -> actual ["cache", "billing"]

(the last line is the probe printing `names = ["cache", "billing"]` against an expectation of `["billing", "dns"]`: removing "cache" deleted "dns" instead and left "cache" in place.) The probe was deleted afterwards, so the shipped crate contains only the four original tests.

also_accept covers Correctness, which is a defensible reading of the same defect at the same location.
